source.stem:
The diagram shows a square ABCD.
M is the midpoint of AB and N is the midpoint of CD.

parts.text: Complete the statement. T he line MN is the locus of points inside the square which are [1]
Shade the region inside the square containing points which are nearer to AB than to BC and nearer to A than to B. [1]

hinge.title: What extra diagonal condition turns the rectangle diagonal construction into a square construction?

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Diagonal is the label that belongs on this item, so 'What extra diagonal condition turns the rectangle diagonal' is answered as diagonal rather than square.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Diagonal is what produces square, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about What extra diagonal condition turns the rectangle.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: square is settled by running 'Is a quadrilateral a kite, and what does its special diagonal do?': A kite can be labelled ABCD with AB = BC and CD = DA; in that kite, diagonal BD bisects — on the item about What extra diagonal condition turns the rectangle.

mx.name: operation_confusion
mx.teacher_note: Square is computed by squaring diagonal and leaving square linear, so the written value is 57 — on the item about What extra diagonal condition turns the rectangle.

intelligence.enrichment: For a square, the diagonals are equal, bisect each other, meet at right angles, and bisect the square's angles.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Mathematics question. Chapter: math/grade_08/ch_104.
